Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the run-chase! United Arab Emirates players are out there in the middle. Johnson Charles and Brandon King are the openers for West Indies. Junaid Siddique to start the proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE …

Right then, West Indies need 203 runs to take a 1-0 lead in this series and we can expect them to take an aggressive route in this run-chase. The pitch though is not easy to bat on and if UAE can find early breakthroughs, they can put pressure on West Indies who are not known to be great against spinners. Stay tuned for the run-chase!

Vriitya Aravind is in for a chat. He says that they had a good partnership and adds that Ali Naseer played well. Mentions that it is not the easiest wicket to bat on and says that they are happy with the total. Reckons that West Indies bowled and fielded well. Feels that they have good varieties in the bowling attack. Shares that he was annoyed after he got out but is happy to get some runs on the board. Ends by saying that they have a good environment to perform.

United Arab Emirates lacked intent throughout the innings. They lost two wickets early and then just went into the shell. Vriitya Aravind played a decent knock of 40 but his wicket triggered a collapse and the UAE middle order just could not find ways to score runs in the middle overs. The debutant, Ali Naseer though mixed caution with aggression beautifully and scored a fifty to take his side to a score where they can at least now fight in the second half of this game.

West Indies bowled with a lot of discipline and the pacers should be credited for the way they bowled on a pitch that had help for the spinners. Both Keemo Paul and Dominic Drakes got a wicket each with the new ball and then the spin duo of Roston Chase and Yannic Cariah just choked UAE's middle order. Yannic Cariah with his crafty leg spin was almost impossible to play at times and started the collapse as UAE crumbled from 100-2 to 145-7. Cariah got two while Chase got one. Keemo Paul and Odean Smith then cleaned up the tail that was starting to frustrate West Indies and overall, it was a comprehensive bowling effort.

United Arab Emirates have managed to cross the 200-run mark but Windies would be happy with their bowling effort. UAE are definitely short of the par score and they need to bowl well here to take a lead in this series. Also, United Arab Emirates missed out on the 17 balls and that would have added some crucial 10-15 runs which might have given them a bit of cushion. Overall, West Indies are favourites to notch up a win going into this break.

The home team, UAE have good blend of youth and experience in their side. Muhammad Waseem and Vriitya Aravind will be key batters for them while the all-round skills of Rohan Mustafa are crucial if they want to upset the Windies here. For the men from the Caribbean, it is about ironing out their flaws and continuing the good work they did in their last ODI series against the Proteas under the leadership of Shai Hope. So, a lot to gain for both teams and expect an exciting encounter. Toss and team news in a bit.

Hello and a very warm welcome, folks! We are all set for a three-match ODI series between the United Arab Emirates and West Indies. We are at the iconic Sharjah Stadium and this is a big opportunity for UAE to show their might in the 50-over format and gain confidence with a good performance in this series. For West Indies, it is an opportunity to try out some new players and they would also like to get some wins under their belt before the all-important World Cup Qualifier. Let’s see how things pan out.
